chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) used to pray two rak'ahs after the 'Isha prayer, reciting one hundred verses in them, and he did not count them [towards the Witr]; and two rak'ahs while sitting, reciting in them 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' and 'Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun'.

If he woke up during the night, he would pray the night prayer and offer Witr; and if he did not wake up until the dawn rose, he would pray two rak'ahs, making them even [Shaf'], and he would count the two rak'ahs he prayed after 'Isha as Witr.

key_terms.شَفْعًا: Even (referring to an even number of rak'ahs)
key_terms.وَتْرًا: Odd (referring to the Witr prayer, which is an odd number of rak'ahs)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq handle the Witr prayer if he slept through the night?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the flexible jurisprudence of Witr prayer in the Shia tradition, highlighting Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) method of ensuring the odd-numbered nature of Witr even when Tahajjud is missed. By designating the post-'Isha prayers as Witr when the night prayer is omitted, the Imam demonstrates a practical application of maintaining the Sunnah's structural integrity. This approach underscores the scholarly emphasis on consistency in voluntary worship while accommodating human limitations such as sleep.
